subject: Science
title: Animals I know
objectives: Children will name familiar animals and say where they see them.
Children will move like different animals.
content: Naming familiar animals, learning where we see them, and moving like animals.
teachingActivities: Use real animals where safe and large pictures or toys otherwise; make the sound and name each animal; link animals to what children see at home and in the compound; never force a child to touch an animal.
learnerActivities: Name familiar animals, say where we see them and move like different animals.
resources: Large animal pictures: dog, cat, goat, hen, cow, lion
A recording of animal sounds if available
assessment: Observe whether each child names at least six animals and moves like an animal on request.
expectedOutcomes: Moves like an animal on request.

lessons.title: Pets and farm animals
lessons.subject: Science
objectives: Children will name a dog, a cat, a goat, a hen and a cow.
successCriteria: Names or points to at least three animals
Makes the sound of an animal
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can explore with their senses, play with water, sand and soil and name the weather.
resources: Large pictures of a dog, cat, goat, hen and cow
lessons.starter: Take the dog picture from the basket and say "Woof, woof. This is a dog. Where do we see dogs?"
teacherActivities: Show each picture, say the animal name and make its sound.
Say a name and ask "Where is the goat?"
Say "Which animal lives at home with us?" and show the pictures.
Let each child hold a toy animal and say its name.
learnerActivities: Children look, point and copy the sound.
Child points to the goat.
Child points to a pet such as a dog or cat.
Child holds the toy and names it.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show each picture, say the animal name and make its sound. Children: Children look, point and copy the sound.
Step 2. Teacher: Say a name and ask "Where is the goat?" Children: Child points to the goat.
Step 3. Teacher: Say "Which animal lives at home with us?" and show the pictures. Children: Child points to a pet such as a dog or cat.
Step 4. Teacher: Let each child hold a toy animal and say its name. Children: Child holds the toy and names it.

practical.title: Animal basket
steps: Put toy animals in a basket.
Each child takes one out and names it.
The group makes its sound together.
practical.safety: Use clean soft toys and wash hands after real animal contact. Never put animals near children’s faces.

differentiation.support: Offer two animals and say the name with the child.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to say where they see the animal.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: What is this animal?
questions.expected: Dog, cat, goat, hen or cow.

lessons.conclusion: Put the animals back in the basket and say each name.
lessons.homeConnection: Name the animals you see at home or on the street with your child.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "name a dog, a cat, a goat, a hen and a cow" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

learnerFacing.songOrRhyme: The dog says woof, the cat says meow, the goat says meh.

lessons.title: Wild animals
lessons.subject: Science
objectives: Children will name wild animals in pictures and say they live outside.
successCriteria: Names or points to a lion, an elephant and a monkey
Says that wild animals live outside
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can explore with their senses, play with water, sand and soil and name the weather.
resources: Large pictures of a lion, an elephant, a monkey and a giraffe
lessons.starter: Show the lion picture and say "Roar! This is a lion. It lives in the wild."
teacherActivities: Show each picture and say the name and what it looks like.
Ask "Which animal is big?" and "Which animal has a long neck?"
Say "Lions and elephants live in the wild. Dogs and goats live with people."
Let each child pick a picture and say a word about it.
learnerActivities: Children look and say the names.
Child points to the elephant or giraffe.
Children listen and nod.
Child shows the picture and says a word.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show each picture and say the name and what it looks like. Children: Children look and say the names.
Step 2. Teacher: Ask "Which animal is big?" and "Which animal has a long neck?" Children: Child points to the elephant or giraffe.
Step 3. Teacher: Say "Lions and elephants live in the wild. Dogs and goats live with people." Children: Children listen and nod.
Step 4. Teacher: Let each child pick a picture and say a word about it. Children: Child shows the picture and says a word.

practical.title: Wild animal pictures
steps: Each child picks a picture and names it.
Make the animal’s sound or movement.
practical.safety: Use pictures or soft toys only. Explain that wild animals are not to be touched and that we look from far away.

differentiation.support: Point to the animal and say the name for the child to copy.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to tell a friend which animal is the biggest.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

expectedOutcomes: Names at least three wild animals
Says that wild animals live outside
lessons.conclusion: Put the pictures away and say "Goodbye, wild animals."
lessons.homeConnection: Look at pictures of wild animals with your child and say their names.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "name wild animals in pictures and say they live outside" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Moving like animals
lessons.subject: Science
objectives: Children will move like different animals.
successCriteria: Moves like at least two animals
Names the animal they are being
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can explore with their senses, play with water, sand and soil and name the weather.
lessons.starter: Show the frog picture and say "Hop like a frog." Hop gently on the spot.
teacherActivities: Show each animal card and demonstrate its movement: hop, crawl, fly, stomp.
Call an animal name and let children move like it.
Play the drum for each animal and stop it for freeze.
Let each child choose an animal card and lead the group.
learnerActivities: Children copy each movement.
Children move like the animal named.
Children move and freeze on the signal.
Child leads and friends copy.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show each animal card and demonstrate its movement: hop, crawl, fly, stomp. Children: Children copy each movement.
Step 2. Teacher: Call an animal name and let children move like it. Children: Children move like the animal named.
Step 3. Teacher: Play the drum for each animal and stop it for freeze. Children: Children move and freeze on the signal.
Step 4. Teacher: Let each child choose an animal card and lead the group. Children: Child leads and friends copy.

practical.title: Animal moves
steps: Clear a space on the mat.
Call out an animal and move like it.
practical.safety: Clear the floor and keep children apart. Keep movements gentle and stop if children are tired.

differentiation.support: Move beside the child and copy together.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to guess which animal a friend is.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

expectedOutcomes: Names the animal they are being
lessons.conclusion: Settle down like a sleeping animal.
lessons.homeConnection: Play animal moves at home and guess each other’s animals.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "move like different animals" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Animal sort
lessons.subject: Science
objectives: Children will sort animals into pets and wild animals.
successCriteria: Puts an animal in the correct group
Says pet or wild with support
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can explore with their senses, play with water, sand and soil and name the weather.
resources: Two hoops labelled pets and wild
lessons.starter: Show two hoops and say "One is for animals that live with us. One is for animals that live in the wild."
teacherActivities: Pick up a dog picture and put it in the pets hoop.
Pick up a lion picture and put it in the wild hoop.
Let each child pick a picture and choose a hoop.
learnerActivities: Children watch and say pet.
Children watch and say wild.
Child places the picture.
Children name the animals in each hoop.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Pick up a dog picture and put it in the pets hoop. Children: Children watch and say pet.
Step 2. Teacher: Pick up a lion picture and put it in the wild hoop. Children: Children watch and say wild.
Step 3. Teacher: Let each child pick a picture and choose a hoop. Children: Child places the picture.
Step 4. Teacher: Check each hoop together. Children: Children name the animals in each hoop.

practical.title: Animal hoops
steps: Put two hoops on the floor.
Place it in the pet or wild hoop.
practical.safety: Use large pictures. Keep the floor clear and supervise turns.

differentiation.support: Offer two pictures and say whether they live with us.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to find another animal for each hoop.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

expectedOutcomes: Sorts animals into pets and wild animals
Says pet or wild with support
lessons.conclusion: Put the pictures away and say "Pets and wild animals."
lessons.homeConnection: Talk about pets and wild animals when you see pictures at home.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "sort animals into pets and wild animals" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Week 1 animals check
lessons.subject: Science
objectives: Teachers will observe how each child names animals and moves like them.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can explore with their senses, play with water, sand and soil and name the weather.
lessons.starter: Sing the animal song and show three stations.
teacherActivities: Set up three stations: naming, sorting and moving.
At each station ask "What animal is this?" and "How does it move?"
Record each child’s level and take photographs.
learnerActivities: Children rotate every four minutes.
Child names the animal or moves.
Children tidy at the signal.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Set up three stations: naming, sorting and moving. Children: Children rotate every four minutes.
Step 2. Teacher: At each station ask "What animal is this?" and "How does it move?" Children: Child names the animal or moves.
Step 3. Teacher: Record each child’s level and take photographs. Children: Children tidy at the signal.

practical.title: Animal stations
practical.safety: Supervise each station and keep floors clear. Use soft toys and large pictures.

differentiation.support: Provide an adult partner and use three animals.
differentiation.extension: Ask a confident child to name all the animals.

assessment.method: Observe and record Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding for: names animals; says where animals live; moves like an animal.

expectedOutcomes: Has an observation record for Week 1
lessons.homeConnection: Name animals together at home or on a walk.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "Teachers will observe how each child names animals and moves like them" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?
